Additive manufacturing, enabling innovation in the orthopedic implant industry
This article covers the benefits of additive manufacturing in the orthopedic implant industry, market potential, and how Freemelt’s e
machine is enabling serial production of titanium orthopedic implants.

In 2023, the market returned to pre-pandemic growth rates, showing a growing demand for various orthopedic devices. By 2032, the orthopedic implant market is expected to reach $86 billion, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5%
. Meanwhile, the 3D printed orthopedic implant market is projected to grow even faster, with an expected CAGR of 16%, reaching $7 billion by the same year

. Several global healthcare companies are at the forefront of this expansion, including, Zimmer Biometh, Stryker, and DePuy Synthes (a Johnson & Johnson company), where Stryker alone has manufactured over 2 million 3D printed implants since 2013
. These industry leaders are continually advancing their offerings, and manufacturing techniques such as additive manufacturing to address the evolving demands of the healthcare sector.
The benefits of additive manufacturing for orthopedic implants
Additive manufacturing has the potential to revolutionize orthopedic implant production, creating new opportunities for innovation and efficiency.

-iM features a high-power electron beam that allows for faster melting and quicker build rates, crucial for industrial serial production.
-iM optimal for manufacturing of orthopedic implants.
